assignments.task_summary: Diagnose and repair one SecurityContext propagation/cleanup seam in asynchronous read-only history projection.
Implement one bounded batch-read service that preserves input correspondence and scope checks for each case reference rather than authorizing only the first.
Minimize a seeded lazy-loading failure where a history DTO accesses an ORM relation after its transaction ends, then repair the read projection boundary.
Implement one result-recording boundary for an existing mock operation so the external mock call occurs outside the SQL transaction and an unknown result keeps its durable reference.
Design and execute a two-writer optimistic-concurrency test against one existing synthetic journey command, including the precise losing response.
Implement and test canonical lock ordering for one existing synthetic operation that touches two permitted records, using bounded opposing request orders.
Write one exception-to-response mapper that distinguishes stale version, bounded contention and unknown mock outcome while preserving safe diagnostics.
Run a small local comparison of the day 17 executor under two declared queue limits and use observed admission/latency/resource evidence to retain one configuration.
Implement one concurrent durable-operation claim seam that distinguishes an exact duplicate request from reuse of the same key with changed revision.
Complete one read-projection integration seam so a committed existing journey transition appears in Support history only with its matching authoritative audit/source reference.
Design and execute the smallest disposable relational projection schema for case-history references, preserving existing event/source identity instead of creating another business ledger.
Implement and test one conditional source-reference constraint that correctly handles SQL UNKNOWN rather than relying on a CHECK that accidentally passes nulls.
Write a scoped history query that admits current assignment without multiplying history rows when historical assignment records exist.
Implement one aggregate projection that includes authorized cases with no events and separates unknown observations from confirmed money effects.
Implement the actual scoped PostgreSQL keyset query matching day 10’s page model, with an explicit fence and bounded page size.
Recreate a scoped keyset query from the input/output contract in a blank query seam, using an unfamiliar assignment history and no prior SQL pasted in.
Implement one cursor-validation/SQL-parameter adapter using the existing approved opaque cursor codec, binding scope, filters, direction and fence.
Write a deterministic SQL display projection for optional source labels while keeping authoritative ordering entirely sequence-based.
Run a two-connection MVCC experiment to define what the history fence does and does not freeze, then choose immutable event snapshot fields for the read contract.
Capture and explain one bounded lock wait involving the history source, then shorten only the unnecessary transaction lifetime in the read adapter.
Find why a seeded left-join aggregate drops an authorized case with no matching events, then repair predicate placement with a minimal fixture.
Generate and interpret an actual PostgreSQL plan for one scoped keyset query on fixed synthetic data, comparing estimates to actual rows without changing indexes yet.
Use day 44’s hypothesis to compare the existing index with at most one candidate index in a disposable fixture, then retain or reject it from matched observations.
Prepare and execute one additive schema change for an optional safe summary code on the disposable read projection, including old-writer/new-reader compatibility.
Implement one resumable, idempotent backfill for the new derived summary code using bounded keyset batches and no rewrites of authoritative events.
Compare offset and keyset access to the same late history page with real plans and exact result equality, then explain where each approach fits.
Implement a bounded transaction retry around one disposable projection-update operation, reopening the transaction for each retry and preserving operation identity.
Complete one SQL-to-Java read adapter for the fenced history page, checking row shape, continuation and safe missing-source representation.
Implement a small state boundary for the history screen that keeps fetched rows in TanStack Query, applied filters in URL state and unapplied filter edits local.
Author typed query-key/options factories for history pages and details from the day 50 contract, including every result-changing scope/filter/fence input.
Implement the history query’s read retry and display-state policy for pending, empty, unavailable, stale-with-data and authorization failure.
Connect the query-provided AbortSignal to the actual history transport and verify cancellation across an applied-filter change.
Implement one controlled filter-editor composition that preserves dirty input across server refresh and deliberately reconciles URL changes.
Fix one optimistic-update race in the existing reversible shortlist seam using serialized or operation-aware reconciliation, then write the counterexample independently.
Implement the URL-to-filter adapter for the history explorer with deterministic normalization, safe defaults and explicit invalid-value feedback.
Implement explicit fenced-page navigation that resets continuation when filter or assignment generation changes and captures a new fence only on deliberate refresh.
Implement one reusable presentational list composition with finite loading/empty/error/ready states and typed row/action slots, leaving fetching in domain hooks.
Implement a row disclosure interaction for the shared history list using native controls, stable accessible names and predictable keyboard/focus behavior.
Implement one source-reference detail dialog using the existing dialog primitive, supplying its task-specific focus, dismissal and unavailable-source behavior.
From a visual/state contract, recreate a small semantic status-badge API with complete static class maps and no copied prior component implementation.
Consume the same typed list composition in the Support history view and an existing owned-journey view using separate prepared domain data adapters.
Refine one responsive history-row layout to keep sequence, outcome and source action understandable at narrow widths and zoom without duplicating markup.
Run a controlled font-load failure/delay experiment on the shared history layout and make one evidence-based fallback adjustment if needed.
Implement one accessible status/error communication seam for history pagination, distinguishing foreground load, background refresh and failed continuation.
Design and implement the invalidation graph for one server-confirmed existing Support event notification, refreshing only affected read keys and resetting obsolete fences.
Minimize a seeded frontend defect where an old Support response writes into unscoped component state after account switch, then remove the unsafe state path.
Run and repair one cross-state interaction sequence combining a dirty filter, pending continuation and later filter replacement using the already authored components.
Use the actual reconciled production build to test every finite shared history/list variant and add the smallest source-detection/static-class fix if a variant is missing.
Inspect the actual current Support public model, map only the case-history read seam and execute a learner-authored contract model for its allowed fields and assignment scope.
Implement the smallest reconciled Spring entry handler that binds authenticated Support scope, parsed filters and the existing history-read service without exposing caller-chosen authority.
